facts.text: The applicant was born in 1926 and lived in İzmir.

anchor.surface_text: 5.  The applicant was born in 1926 and lived in İzmir.

facts.text: On 23 February 1998 the applicant bought a plot of land (plot no. 536 in the Ulucak village, in the Menemen district of İzmir) from the heirs of V.G.

anchor.surface_text: 6.  On 23 February 1998 the applicant bought a plot of land (plot no. 536 in the Ulucak village, in the Menemen district of İzmir) from the heirs of V.G.

facts.text: On 13 July 1999 the Ministry of Agriculture brought an action before the Menemen Civil Court requesting annulment of the applicant's title deed to plot no. 536 and its registration in the Treasury's name, claiming actual possession since 1966 and relying on Article 38 of the Expropriation Act (Law no. 2942).

anchor.surface_text: 7.  On 13 July 1999 the Ministry of Agriculture (“the Ministry”) brought an action before the Menemen Civil Court, requesting the annulment of the title deed of the applicant to plot no. 536 and its registration in the Treasury's name, claiming that it had had actual possession of this land since 1966. The Ministry primarily relied on Article 38 of the Expropriation Act (Law no. 2942). The Ministry also alleged that an expropriation had been effected in relation to the said land in 1966 and that V.G. had received compensation for it. However, the land register had not been amended due to an administrative error.

facts.text: On 20 December 2000 the Menemen Civil Court accepted the Ministry's request and ordered the land to be registered in favour of the Treasury under Article 38 of Law no. 2942, noting the Ministry's actual possession for over twenty years and the applicant's awareness of this when buying the plot.

anchor.surface_text: 8.  On 20 December 2000 the Menemen Civil Court accepted the request of the Ministry of Agriculture and ordered that the land be registered in favour of the Treasury in accordance with Article 38 of Law no. 2942. In its judgment, the first-instance court noted that the Ministry had been in actual possession of this land for more than twenty years and that the applicant had been aware of this fact when he had bought the plot.

facts.text: The applicant appealed the Menemen Civil Court's decision.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  The applicant appealed.

facts.text: On 17 September 2001 the Court of Cassation upheld the judgment of 20 December 2000.

anchor.surface_text: 10.  On 17 September 2001 the Court of Cassation upheld the judgment of 20 December 2000.

facts.text: The applicant requested rectification of the Court of Cassation's decision of 17 September 2001.

anchor.surface_text: 11.  The applicant requested rectification of the decision of 17 September 2001.

facts.text: On 24 December 2001 the Court of Cassation dismissed the applicant's request for rectification.

anchor.surface_text: 12.  On 24 December 2001 the Court of Cassation dismissed the applicant's request.

facts.text: On 4 January 2002 the Court of Cassation's decision was served on the applicant.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  On 4 January 2002 the Court of Cassation's decision was served on the applicant.

facts.text: On 10 April 2003 the Constitutional Court annulled Article 38 of Law no. 2942.

anchor.surface_text: 14.  On 10 April 2003 the Constitutional Court annulled Article 38 of Law no. 2942.

facts.text: The Government maintained that the plot had been expropriated in 1966 and compensation paid to V.G., the owner at the time, and submitted a 13 September 1966 document notifying V.G. of the expropriation decision and compensation deposit.

anchor.surface_text: 20.  The Government maintained that the impugned plot had been expropriated in 1966 and compensation had been paid to V.G., the owner of the land at the material time. In view of this expropriation, which had been effected long before its purchase by the applicant, the Government argued that the applicant had never had a legitimate property right to the land in question. To support their allegations, the Government submitted a document dated 13 September 1966, which notified V.G. through the notary public of the expropriation decision and further informed him that the relevant compensation would be deposited at a public bank.

facts.text: The applicant contested the Government's claim, arguing the expropriation was never completed as compensation was never deposited and the title deed register was never amended in favour of the Treasury.

anchor.surface_text: 21.  The applicant contested these submissions. He argued that the expropriation of the plot had never been completed as alleged by the Government as the expropriation compensation had never been deposited with the bank and hence the title deed register had never been amended in favour of the Treasury.

facts.text: The Court found no evidence that any payment was made to finalise the expropriation and concluded there was insufficient evidence that the land was effectively expropriated by the Ministry at any point.

anchor.surface_text: 22.  The Court observes in the first place that despite its allegations concerning the expropriation of the disputed plot, the Government cannot produce any evidence to prove that any payment was made in relation to this expropriation to finalise it. In these circumstances, and bearing in mind the ownership status at the title deed register prior to the judgment of the Menemen Civil Court on 20 December 2000, the Court believes that there is not enough evidence to conclude that the impugned land was effectively expropriated by the Ministry at any point.

facts.text: The Court concluded the applicant was the legal owner of the disputed land until the Menemen Civil Court judgment and was deprived of his land pursuant only to section 38 of Law no. 2942.

anchor.surface_text: 23.  Secondly, the Court observes that regardless of whether any expropriation was effected in 1966 or not, the Menemen Civil Court relied on no reasons other than section 38 of Law no. 2942 in ordering the registration of the land in favour of the Treasury. In these circumstances, the Court cannot but conclude that the applicant was the legal owner of the disputed land up until the judgment of the Menemen Civil Court and that he was deprived of his land within the meaning of Article 1 of Protocol No. 1, pursuant only to section 38 of Law no. 2942.

facts.text: Section 38 of Law no. 2942 required compensation applications within twenty years of property occupation; national courts applied this retrospectively, depriving the applicant of compensation possibility.

anchor.surface_text: 24.  In this connection, the Court notes that according to section 38 of Law no. 2942, applications for compensation for deprivation of property had to be made within twenty years of the date the property was occupied. By applying this provision retrospectively, the national courts deprived the applicant of any possibility of obtaining compensation for the annulment of his title deed.

facts.text: Since the application was lodged, section 38 of Law no. 2942 was annulled by the Constitutional Court as unconstitutional for arbitrarily depriving individuals of property rights and compensation.

anchor.surface_text: The Court observes at this point that, since the application was lodged with the Court, section 38 of Law no. 2942 has been annulled by the Constitutional Court as being unconstitutional. In its judgment dated 10 April 2003, the Constitutional Court held that limiting an individual's right to property, by maintaining that the right to bring an action against the de facto occupation of the disputed property lapses, and requiring that the property must be transferred to the authorities twenty years after that occupation, was contrary to the Constitution. Moreover, referring to the case-law of the Court, it held that depriving individuals arbitrarily of their right to property and their right to compensation was contrary to the principle of the rule of law.

facts.text: The Constitutional Court's judgment did not have retroactive effect and did not provide the applicant with a procedure to redress the violation effects.

anchor.surface_text: 25.  The Court takes into consideration the judgment of the Constitutional Court and acknowledges its reasoning. Nevertheless, it notes that the judgment of the Constitutional Court did not have retroactive effect and therefore did not provide the applicant with a procedure capable of redressing the effects of a possible violation of the Convention.
